title: Model-building-first AI roadmap
calendar_note: Day numbers are study-day positions; dates are planning dates, never evidence or deadlines.

feasibility.initial_model_to_product_progression_est: 25–39 active study weeks (175–273 daily study units if studying every day); estimate is conditional and includes foundations, training, evaluation, integration and evidence, not just coding.
feasibility.nine_month_target: One strong end-to-end CoverStory flagship plus model-training experiments, conditional on held-out evidence; StreamForge and Developer Workflow Assistant remain later work.
feasibility.three_flagship_horizon: 12–18 months is a planning range; this calendar uses 548 days (18 months) with recovery time inside the fixed budget.

phases.focus: Python, NumPy, probability/linear algebra fundamentals, gradient intuition, data hygiene and first baselines
phases.exit: Can reproduce a tiny model update, explain loss/gradient, preserve held-out isolation, compare simple baselines with independent metrics.

phases.focus: Classical ML, evaluation slices, leakage prevention, uncertainty, feature design and reusable evaluation harness
phases.exit: Multiple fixed-label experiments with reproducible train/validation/test splits, baseline comparisons and counterfactual/error slices.

phases.focus: PyTorch tensors/autograd/training loops/optimization; small CPU neural models; tiny educational transformer
phases.exit: Reproducible small-model training, ablations, held-out metrics, runtime/memory limits and honest limitations; not frontier pretraining.

phases.focus: Tokenization, pretrained model use, fine-tuning readiness and license/compute/data checks; CoverStory integration starts earlier only after model baseline/held-out gates
phases.exit: A justified small-model adaptation or explicit no-go based on baseline, license, compute and held-out evaluation; integrated CoverStory has source-grounded tests.

phases.focus: Harden the CoverStory integration that starts after model readiness around Day 211; complete retrieval, citations, permission boundaries, abstention, evaluations and supplied app infrastructure
phases.exit: Reproducible offline evaluation, error/security slices, model/data card, and live-provider evidence only if separately authorized and genuinely observed.

phases.focus: Train/evaluate a recommender or ranker with public/synthetic data and supplied platform plumbing
phases.exit: Held-out ranking comparison against simple baselines; cold-start/fairness/failure analysis; no fabricated usage claims.

phases.focus: Train/evaluate a bounded classification/ranking capability in the Developer Workflow Assistant with read-only-first tool use
phases.exit: Task outcomes, injection/permission tests, failure recovery and measured comparison; writes remain approval-gated.

phases.focus: Reuse evaluation/observability across all three projects, recovery, portfolio and readiness review
phases.exit: Reproducible artifact inventory and limitations; no automatic readiness, certification, role or adoption claim.

application_comprehension_and_scalabilit.budget_policy: Within existing engineering/shared allocations; supplied app and bounded local load harnesses only. No external load generation or added hours.
application_comprehension_and_scalabilit.learner_work: Read/trace supplied FE/BE/HLD/LLD code, diagnose seeded failures, answer question-bank prompts, and interpret measured results. No standalone UI/API/auth/CRUD/DevOps implementation or capstone design essay.

topics_by_project_need.topics: request/data-flow trace, array/model memory and local batch inference; declared local concurrency and p50/p95/error measurement.

retrieval/query indexes; permission and API contract walkthrough; FE rendering/state/network/caching/streaming/large lists; bounded batch inference; latency, memory, throughput, quality and cost trade-offs.

ranking throughput, caching with Redis only if repeated reads justify it (TTL, invalidation, rate limits, atomicity/failure); Kafka only if asynchronous event flow is justified (partitions, consumer groups, order, replay, lag, delivery guarantees/idempotency). Compare simpler alternatives first.
tool/API boundaries, queues and durable recovery; idempotency, backpressure, retries/timeouts, authorization, safe approval and replay; no write-capable live connector without separate authorization.

topics_by_project_need.stage: Platform integration days 301–548 as prerequisites permit
topics_by_project_need.topics: assistant-supplied container/CI/CD/IaC walkthroughs, secrets boundary, rollout/rollback, monitoring and incident scenarios; Kubernetes only after a simpler deployment is understood and justified. MLOps: dataset/model versioning, reproducible training, experiment tracking/registry, evaluation gates, deployment/readiness, drift and retraining.

application_comprehension_and_scalabilit.measurement_contract: Any local load result states hardware/runtime, dataset, concurrency, duration, p50/p95, error rate and resource bounds; no test is described as global or production scale.

project_gates.gate: Enter only after model baseline and separate held-out evaluation; document ingestion/provenance; retrieval/citation/abstention checks; tenant and data-governance tests; repeatable demo. Day 274 review targets one coherent end-to-end vertical slice plus measured model experiments, conditional on evidence. Live provider and production gates remain unmet without authorized real evidence.
Ranking/recommendation model compared to trivial baseline on held-out public/synthetic examples; cold-start and relevant fairness/error slices; reproducible results.

project_gates.entry: StreamForge evidence gate passed, or bounded recovery plan recorded; preserve work on both project threads within capacity.
project_gates.gate: Measured task-success evaluation, read-only default, explicit approval for any write path, injection/authorization/recovery controls.

project_gates.entry: Prior project results are available; unresolved gates remain explicitly open and receive bounded recovery.
project_gates.gate: Same reusable evaluation schema applied to three distinct model capabilities with independent expected outputs and preserved limitations.

milestone_reviews.gate: Python/math/classical ML, clean held-out split, independently checked baselines; no title or job-readiness inference.

milestone_reviews.target: AI Product / Applied AI SWE portfolio checkpoint
milestone_reviews.gate: One strong CoverStory vertical slice plus model experiments only if actual held-out and integration evidence qualifies; applications may begin earlier.
Grounding, retrieval/citations, permissions, abstention, evaluation and honest live-provider status; no automatic completion.
Held-out ranking against baseline, cold-start/failure slices and reproducible metrics; no fabricated adoption.

milestone_reviews.target: Developer Workflow Assistant and later FDE evidence checkpoint
milestone_reviews.gate: Measured tool-task outcomes and safe permissions; FDE evidence additionally requires real external discovery/stakeholder delivery/adoption.
Review each project and open external/production gates; no role, title, certification, mastery or professional ownership claim.
Requires externally verified sustained ownership, technical influence, adoption, cross-team impact and review; distinct from the learning calendar.
